resources.string: Enable Android accessibility access to start blocking.
Keep regular videos, block the Shorts viewer.
Keep posts and messages, block the Reels viewer.
Home and Explore count. Messages and profiles pause the timer.
First limit reached: Instagram is blocked for 30 minutes. Second time that day: blocked until midnight.
Opening a Short or Reel blocks the entire application for 30 minutes.
A new attempt does not restart or extend the countdown.
When a Short or Reel is detected, Anti Scroll presses Back and displays a focus reminder. Nothing you view is stored or sent.
When a Short or Reel is detected, the entire platform is blocked for 30 minutes. Attempts during the penalty display the remaining time.
The Instagram timer runs only while the feed is in the foreground. It pauses in messages and profiles, and a session resets when you leave Instagram.

Anti Scroll uses Android accessibility access to identify YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels, and whether Instagram is showing the feed, messages, or a profile. It uses Back to leave blocked content or a sanctioned application without changing the current launcher page. The optional session limit counts feed time and can block Instagram for 30 minutes, then until midnight after a second overrun. Interface content is never stored or transmitted.
Detects YouTube Shorts and Instagram Reels, can limit Instagram feed sessions, and returns to the previous screen when access is blocked. All processing stays on this device.
